text:
alex: heads up — EverWell POC just cut the streaming response in their desktop kiosk. Customer says output stops halfway through JSON object and their renderer throws "Unexpected end of input". Happened during a demo with clinician notes generation (~3m mark). req id: req_1b2c3d
junaid: Thanks. Which runtime/model and SDK?
alex: hosted model gpt-4o-stream-v1, desktop-sdk v1.2.0 (electron wrapper). Customer kiosk runs Windows 10 with embedded Edge WebView2.
erin: Do we have the raw SSE chunks or headers? Ask them for the full HTTP response headers from their proxy/gateway.
mark: I grabbed headers and a small tcpdump. Gateway is an IIS+ARR farm that adds `Content-Encoding: gzip` and a `Content-Length: 0` header before forwarding to the kiosk. Also saw `X-ARR-LOG-ID: 0e4f`.
junaid: That combo is suspicious. gzip + chunked streaming often results in buffering if the proxy tries to buffer to compute content-length. Does ARR enable response buffering by default?
erin: Yes ARR sometimes does. Also Edge WebView2 mishandles incrementally flushed gzip streams when the proxy alters headers. Can we repro from our side by putting ARR in front of the stream?
junaid: Try curl with --no-buffer and show headers: ```curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?req=req_1b2c3d``` Look at `Transfer-Encoding` and `Content-Encoding`.
alex: I ran curl from my laptop against their gateway and saw the same truncation. Repro confirmed. Kernel-level packet shows server kept sending but gateway closed the connection with FIN after approx 2.7MB.
erin: Two action items: 1) Customer change: disable response buffering / compression for SSE endpoints in ARR (set proxyPreserveHost and disable compression so ARR doesn't buffer to compute Content-Length). 2) Our side: add periodic non-gzip keepalive SSE comment lines (`:keepalive

`) and smaller flush window (reduce streaming_chunk_size to 64 bytes) as short-term mitigation.
unj: (typo) junaid: Also make sure client app is parsing SSE properly: don't assume each `data:` contains complete JSON; accumulate until you hit a blank line. Older Electron versions sometimes call `onmessage` per chunk.
mark: Customer said they can't remove gzip due to corporate gateway policy. They can whitelist the endpoint and set `enableResponseBuffering=false` in ARR.
erin: If they must keep gzip, ask them to enable streaming-friendly compression (brotli/deflate with chunked streaming) and ensure ARR does not attempt to buffer to compute Content-Length. Provide ARR docs snippet.
junaid: I'll draft an ARR config snippet and an example tcpdump grep to find `FIN` events: `sudo tcpdump -w capture.pcap -s 0 host X.X.X.X and port 443` then open in Wireshark.
alex: Created quick assist ticket POC-4891 and toggled a tenant-side patch to flush every 128 bytes for this demo. ops-bot: ticket created: POC-4891 assigned to junaid and erin. Link: https://redwood.support/tickets/POC-4891
mark: Re-tested after we disabled ARR buffering on their staging gateway. Stream persisted and client no longer hit parse error in a 15-minute run. A few residual partial-utf8 artifacts on older WebView2 builds — our devs will upgrade runtime.
erin: Great. Follow-ups: - Send ARR config snippet + curl repro instructions - Recommend client-side SSE parsing best-practices (accumulate, handle partial UTF-8) - Keep tenant-side increased flush as fallback while customer upgrades gateway.
alex: Thanks team — passing back to AE for closure. Blocker resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
